skill.name: managing-workflow
skill.description: Guides a specification-driven development workflow for software features. It loads .spec artifacts, validates phase gates, creates planning templates, tracks progress, and archives completed work.
skill.summary: Guide software features from specification through planning, implementation, validation, and archive.
skill.author: BrendanShields

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, Bash examples, or JavaScript template literals. The real risk is unvalidated path arguments in helper scripts. They can read, write, append to, or move workflow files; no network exfiltration or prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated path arguments in helper scripts
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths with path.resolve, reject absolute paths and traversal, and enforce containment under the project .spec directory before filesystem operations.

remediation.issue: Freeform status and metric text is written to artifacts
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist workflow status values and escape Markdown table separators, newlines, and control characters in activity events.
Require CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to resolve inside the active workspace before loading workflow context.
Document required tools and ask for user confirmation before archive or status-changing commands run.

content.value_statement: Feature work can lose scope, status, and review checkpoints across long sessions. This skill guides specification, planning, tasks, validation, and archiving with local artifacts.
actual_capabilities: Loads current workflow context from .spec artifacts.
Detects the active phase from feature frontmatter and artifacts.
Guides specification, planning, task creation, implementation, validation, and archiving.
Provides quick plan and quick task templates for small changes.
Updates feature status, progress, and activity metrics through helper scripts.
Validates required artifacts before phase transitions.
limitations: Requires a .spec directory structure with expected Markdown artifacts.
Needs shell access to run its local Node.js helper scripts.
Does not judge product quality beyond artifact completeness.
Implementation work is delegated to other agents or the active coding tool.

use_cases.title: Start a Feature With Clear Scope
use_cases.description: Create a feature specification, acceptance criteria, and tracking files before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Review Gates
use_cases.description: Move work through specification, planning, tasks, and implementation with explicit approval points.

use_cases.title: Resume Long AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Load current status from artifacts and continue from the correct workflow phase.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-workflow skill to start a new feature for: [short feature description]. Ask me for any missing scope details.

prompt_templates.title: Create the Technical Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-workflow skill to review the current spec, resolve any clarification tags, and create a technical plan.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Implementation Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an approved plan into work items
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-workflow skill to validate the plan and create implementation tasks with dependencies and priority labels.

prompt_templates.title: Validate and Archive Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the managing-workflow skill to validate completion, update progress, identify repeatable tooling opportunities, and archive the feature if approved.

output_examples.input: Start a new feature for password reset emails.
output_examples.output: Creates a scoped feature record, asks for missing requirements, drafts user stories, and prepares review-ready specification artifacts.

output_examples.input: Continue the active checkout redesign work.
output_examples.output: Loads the current feature status, identifies the next phase, and recommends the next required action before implementation.

output_examples.input: This feature is done. Close it out.
output_examples.output: Checks remaining tasks, updates completion status, logs activity, and offers to archive the completed feature.

best_practices: Review each generated artifact before approving the next phase.
Keep feature names short and path-safe before creating artifacts.
Use the quick templates only for small, low-risk changes.
anti_patterns: Skipping plan and task artifacts before implementation.
Marking work complete while unchecked tasks remain.
Using vague feature descriptions that cannot produce testable acceptance criteria.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages a specification-driven workflow for software features using local Markdown artifacts.

faq.question: Does it write code for the feature?
faq.answer: It prepares and validates the workflow. Actual implementation is delegated to the active coding tool or another agent.

faq.question: What files does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects feature artifacts such as spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, and metrics.md under a .spec directory.

faq.question: Can it handle small fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes quick plan and quick task templates for simple changes.

faq.question: Does it require shell commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Its helper scripts are Node.js commands that read or update local workflow artifacts.

faq.question: Can it archive completed work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can move completed feature artifacts into the archive flow after validation and user approval.
